commands.description: Grant or revoke Claude agent access to your Design projects

commands.name: design-sync
commands.description: Push a React design system to claude.ai/design. This runs a converter that bundles the real component code (from Storybook or a bare package) and uploads it. Use when the user runs /design-sync or says "sync my design system to Claude Design".

commands.name: dataviz
commands.description: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. When the destination is a first-party document connector (host-designated, never self-described) that renders live charts, hand it the rows (inline, or as an uploaded data file the chart cites) rather than a rendered PNG/SVG — a picture of a chart loses hover, data inspection and per-value comments. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".

commands.name: update-config
commands.description: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.

commands.name: verify
commands.description: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Run before committing nontrivial changes; bootstraps this repo's project verify skill if none exists yet. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.

commands.name: debug
commands.description: Enable debug logging for this session and help diagnose issues

commands.name: code-review
commands.description: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs (plus reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups where the model's review recipe covers them) at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.

commands.name: simplify
commands.description: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.

commands.name: batch
commands.description: Research and plan a large-scale change, then execute it in parallel across 5–30 isolated worktree agents that each open a PR.

commands.name: fewer-permission-prompts
commands.description: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.

commands.name: doctor
commands.description: Health-check the user's Claude Code setup and fix issues: diagnose installation health — what the `claude doctor` terminal diagnostics cover — from local data (duplicate or leftover installs, PATH, unparseable settings files, broken or colliding agent definitions, skills whose frontmatter fails to parse); find unused skills, MCP servers, and plugins versus their context cost and disable dead weight; deduplicate local CLAUDE.md files against checked-in ones; trim checked-in CLAUDE.md files by cutting content a session could derive from the codebase (directory layouts, tech-stack lists, architecture overviews) while keeping gotchas, rationale, and non-standard conventions; migrate always-loaded CLAUDE.md guidance into lazy skills and nested CLAUDE.md files; flag slow hooks and context-heavy extensions; check the installed version is current; make auto mode the default permission mode; and pre-approve frequently denied read-only commands. Use when the user asks for a doctor run, checkup, audit, tune-up, or cleanup of their Claude Code setup or configuration.

commands.name: loop
commands.description: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace.

commands.name: schedule
commands.description: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule.

commands.name: claude-api
commands.description:
Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).

commands.name: workflow-authoring
commands.description: Reference for writing a Workflow tool script (script API and gotchas, resume, quality patterns, worked examples). Load before authoring a script for a workflow the user already opted into; it does not itself authorize running one.

commands.name: run
commands.description: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

commands.name: run-skill-generator
commands.description: Author or improve the run-<unit> skill - a per-project skill that tells agents how to build, launch, and drive this project's app. Use when the user asks to set up the project, get it running, write run instructions, or verify build/run steps work from a clean environment.

commands.name: docs
commands.description: docs (editable docs people share and comment on; the default for any document, named as a doc or not: a document, report, proposal, resume, cover letter, letter, contract, policy, form, template, worksheet, essay, handbook, guide, how-to, cheat sheet, SOP or other writing to keep, share, collaborate on, send, submit, print or sign; a doc exports to Word, PDF, Markdown or Google Docs, so needing a file to send, attach, upload, submit or print is no reason to pick Word, and a file nobody asked for is a doc, not Word; a plan, comparison, summary or notes asked in chat stays in chat; a pasted claude.ai artifact link may be a doc: check with docs tools first; Word or another file format named, tracked changes wanted, or a .docx to change or use as a template → that format's skill): making one → if no docs-connector instructions are in context, call its `guide` (topic.instructions) first; then create the doc (headings only, no body) before any search, file read or plan, even with files attached. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: docx
commands.description: Use this skill whenever the user wants to create, read, edit, or manipulate Word documents (.docx) or Word templates (.dotx). Triggers include: any mention of Microsoft Word Documents, such as 'Word doc', 'word document', '.docx', '.dotx', 'microsoft doc'. Also use when extracting or reorganizing content from .docx or .dotx files, inserting or replacing images in documents, find-and-replace in Word files, working with tracked changes or comments, or converting content into a polished Word document. If the user asks for a deliverable as a Word or .docx file (to download, email or print), use this skill. However, if they ask for a document, page, report, memo, or notes WITHOUT naming a file format and the session offers Claude's own dedicated document or page skill or connector, use that instead, even if they will email or print it. Do NOT use for PDFs, spreadsheets, Google Docs, or coding unrelated to document generation. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: google-workspace
commands.description: Read this before the first Google Drive, Docs, Sheets or Slides connector call whenever the task creates or changes a Google file. Use this skill whenever the user wants to create or change a Google Doc, Sheet or Slides file in their Google Drive. Triggers include: a request that names Google Docs, Sheets, Slides or Drive and asks to make, edit, format, copy or rename a file; a docs.google.com link with a request to change that file, even a one-line fix or suggested edits; and any follow-up change to a Google file from earlier in the chat, even "change it" or "add a tab". Includes helper scripts for document positions, cell ranges and slide layout. However, if the user asks for a doc, deck or spreadsheet without naming Google, or gives a Google file only as source material for something new, use Claude's own output type instead. Do NOT use for read-only questions about a Google file, or for Word, Excel, PowerPoint or PDF files. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: import-memory
commands.description: Import a memory export from another AI assistant into Claude's memory — conversationally, additively, and with the content treated as data. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: morning
commands.description: Render the user's morning brief as a styled HTML artifact, or set it up as a recurring weekday task. Use only when the user explicitly asks to run, see, or set up their morning brief, or if they invoke /morning by name. A question about their day, schedule, or calendar is not by itself a request for the brief; answer it directly instead. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: pdf
commands.description: Use this skill whenever the user wants to do anything with PDF files. This includes reading or extracting text/tables from PDFs, combining or merging multiple PDFs into one, splitting PDFs apart, rotating pages, adding watermarks, creating new PDFs, filling PDF forms, encrypting/decrypting PDFs, extracting images, and OCR on scanned PDFs to make them searchable. If the user mentions a .pdf file or asks to produce one, use this skill. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: pptx
commands.description: Use this skill any time a .pptx or .potx file is involved in any way — as input, output, or both. This includes: creating slide decks, pitch decks, or presentations as PowerPoint (.pptx) files; reading, parsing, or extracting text from any .pptx or .potx file (even if the extracted content will be used elsewhere, like in an email, summary, or creating a different type of slide deck); editing, modifying, or updating existing presentations; combining or splitting slide files; working with templates (.potx), layouts, speaker notes, or comments. Trigger whenever the user asks for a PowerPoint or .pptx file, or references a .pptx or .potx filename, regardless of what they plan to do with the content afterward. However, when the user asks for a deck, slides, a slide deck, or a presentation without naming a file format, default to using a dedicated slide-deck artifact type or a separate slides skill if this session offers one; otherwise, use this skill. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: skill-creator
commands.description: Create new skills, modify and improve existing skills, and measure skill performance. Use when users want to create a skill from scratch, edit, or optimize an existing skill, run evals to test a skill, benchmark skill performance with variance analysis, or optimize a skill's description for better triggering accuracy. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: xlsx
commands.description: Use this skill any time a spreadsheet file is the primary input or output. This means any task where the user wants to: open, read, edit, or fix an existing .xlsx, .xlsm, .xltx, .csv, or .tsv file (e.g., adding columns, computing formulas, formatting, charting, cleaning messy data); create a new spreadsheet from scratch or from other data sources; or convert between tabular file formats. Trigger especially when the user references a spreadsheet file by name or path — even casually (like "the xlsx in my downloads") — and wants something done to it or produced from it. Also trigger for cleaning or restructuring messy tabular data files (malformed rows, misplaced headers, junk data) into proper spreadsheets. The deliverable must be a spreadsheet file. Do NOT trigger when the primary deliverable is a Word document, HTML report, standalone Python script, database pipeline, or Google Sheets API integration, even if tabular data is involved. (claude.ai sync)

# Review of a specification repair and two search protocols (frozen)

A researcher repaired a specification against defects D1–D14 (REVIEW-1bb.md) and froze two search protocols (TASK.md, HUMAN-DECISIONS.md); the output is SPEC-r1.md / SPEC-r1.json / CHANGELOG.md. Use only these files.

Check each of the following:
1. **Each defect D1–D14:** is the correction real and sufficient, or cosmetic? Is any defect left unaddressed? Is any **new** defect introduced?
2. **D1 especially:** does the corrected spec avoid presenting any observation explainable by both hypotheses as a discriminator? Is the required independent norm-state observable specified per prediction?
3. **Six distinctions:** are they kept separate throughout (norm exists / in force / known in force / act according to / act contrary to / change without act)?
4. **Does the corrected spec now smuggle in H-B** (overcorrection), or does it still smuggle in H-D?
5. **Rank-0 protocol:** can it be executed deterministically and reproduced? Is the target matching over- or under-inclusive? Is "execution trace" vs "mention" operational? Is M-TIME respected (no timestamp used for decision or effectiveness)? Is absence handled as NOT-EVIDENCED-IN-CAPTURE?
6. **Scoping protocol:** existence-only, bounded, with explicit independence and completeness criteria?

Verdict: **PASS** · **PASS_WITH_LIMITATIONS** · **FAIL**, with the exact defects. **A protocol with a FAIL must not be executed.**

Classify each issue as: wording · source interpretation · coding · evidence scope · independence · formal reasoning · substantive.

Write **REVIEW.md** and **REVIEW.json** ({verdict, defects_status: {D1..D14: FIXED | PARTIAL | NOT_FIXED}, new_defects: [...], d1_assessment, smuggling: {HD, HB}, rank0_protocol: {executable, issues: [...]}, scoping_protocol: {bounded, issues: [...]}, disagreements: [...]}).

1	# REVIEW of SPEC.md / SPEC.json (adversarial)
2	
3	Inputs used: TASK.md, HYPOTHESES.md, IDENTIFIABILITY.json, CONFORMANCE-CASE.json, STATE.md, SPEC.md, SPEC.json. Nothing else.
4	
5	## Verdict: **PASS_WITH_LIMITATIONS**
6	
7	The spec does most of what TASK.md asks, and does it carefully:
8	- It keeps to the scope IDENTIFIABILITY.json allows: it drops P3 and P6 and states that P2, P4 and P5 are one-sided.
9	- It removes the draft's unexplained "≥3" and "2 pairs" minimums and gives a reason for each replacement.
10	- It replaces the "complete act log including unregistered ones" with a closed channel.
11	- It adds windows, and it hedges the feasibility section.
12	
13	It does not reach PASS. Its headline deliverable, the "single smallest discriminating acquisition", is defective as stated:
14	- One of its three outcome branches does not separate the hypotheses (D1).
15	- The three items are not enough to trigger the falsifiers the spec itself defines (D2).
16	- It leaves out the outcome where no WP-4C-1 work exists (D2).
17	- Its claim to be the only small two-sided acquisition contradicts the spec's own P5 entry (D3).
18	
19	The closed-world register is also under-defined (D5), and the P7 window starts at a recording time (D4).
20	
21	All of these can be fixed without redoing the per-prediction work, so the verdict is not FAIL. **The ranking and the smallest-acquisition section should not be used until D1–D5 are fixed.**
22	
23	## Defects (most severe first)
24	
25	| # | Class | Where | Defect | Fix |
26	|---|---|---|---|---|
27	| **D1** | formal reasoning | §5 branch 1; P4 H-D falsifier; P5; P1 H-D | **The same observation serves both sides.** "R-89 not adopted, but work ran under it" is read as H-D's status clause failing. 285	  - The P7-HB falsifier says "gate in force". Without the field, it could fire against a gate that was not in force.
286	  - P5-HD needs the capability norm at the time R-94 was made, not the capability norm as it is now.
287	  - The P1 census needs eligibility to be decided by a rule, not after the fact. P1's D1 split needs to know whether a later act legitimated the apparent change.
288	  - P8-HB is conditioned on "active target".
289	- Adding the premise as a field makes each falsifier's condition checkable.
290	
291	**(4) Does it change a scientific prediction?** Yes, at the operational level.
292	- **P7-HB:** cannot fire unless R-72's gate is in force at t_w.
293	- **P5-HD:** judged against the capability norm in force at t_R94.
294	- **P1:** the census is limited to targets that are eligible under the frozen criterion. An apparent act-less change followed by a legitimating act is scored as legitimated, not as a norm change without an act.
295	- **P8-HB:** limited to targets that are active under the frozen definition.
296	
297	**(5) Frozen rule.**
298	> **FR-D8.**
299	> - P7-HB requires `r72_gate_in_force_at_t_w` = IN_FORCE (NIF, or the graded fallback).
300	> - P5-HD requires `capability_norm_in_force_at_t_R94`.
301	> - A P1 target is **eligible** iff a norm-making act recorded before t1 made its deontic state conditional on a stated work condition, and a system-recorded artefact inside W shows that condition met under a satisfaction rule written per clause before Stage 1.
302	> - P1 records `response_or_legitimation`: any later act that ratifies, sanctions or reverses the apparent change, with its time.
303	> - A P8 target is **active** at t iff an authorization on it is in force at t (NIF or fallback), and no closure, acceptance, withdrawal or hold act on it is in force at t.
304	
305	---
306	
307	## D9: the C1 rule is asymmetric and under-specified
308	
309	**(1) Defect, quoted.**
310	> "The C1 rule will probably return UNDETERMINED, and it is asymmetric. If R-72's proviso was unmet but no blocking text covers RED, the rule says UNDETERMINED. By R-72's own logic the conditional authorization never became operative, so the result should be NON-CONFORMS by default. No default reading of 'WP-4B REMAINS BLOCKED' is fixed for the likely case where no scoping text exists. Entry-into-force times for R-77 to R-80 are to come 'from adoption records', but these rulings may not be status-mediated at all, and no fallback is given. The MD and the JSON also scope the 'and' in the CONFORMS branch differently."
311	
312	**(2) Correction.** (§2)
313	- **Default state:** WP-4B work is UNAUTHORIZED at 16:10 unless R-72's proviso is *shown* met, by texts in force before 16:10.
314	- **Default scope:** "WP-4B REMAINS BLOCKED" covers all WP-4B work, including producer-agnostic RED test code, unless a text in force before 16:10 explicitly narrows it.
315	- **Fallback for rulings that are not status-mediated:** entry into force is not earlier than the ruling's recording time, graded by §0.9. A stated date is SOURCE_STATED.
316	- **One structure** for CONFORMS: **P ∧ ¬B**. The MD version is kept, because R-72's authorization and R-77's block are separate conditions, and both must be satisfied.
317	- **UNDETERMINED** is reserved for two cases:
318	  - required texts cannot be obtained;
319	  - the time at which a relevant text entered force, relative to 16:10, is NOT_IDENTIFIABLE.
320	- If the texts are obtained and do not show the proviso met, the result is NON-CONFORMS by default.
321	
322	**(3) Why this is sufficient.**
323	- **Asymmetry removed.** The default follows R-72's own conditional form: an authorization that is conditional on a proviso is operative only if the proviso holds. So the case "proviso unmet, no covering block" now yields NON-CONFORMS.
324	- **Default scope fixed.** The case with no scoping text now has a determinate reading.
325	- **Fallback added.** Rulings without an adoption record now have a time premise.
326	- **Consistency.** A single boolean structure makes the MD and the JSON identical.
327	- **Guard against unseen evidence.** UNDETERMINED remains only where a premise is actually unobservable. So the default is never applied to evidence that has not been seen: missing texts give UNDETERMINED, not NON-CONFORMS.
328	
329	**(4) Does it change a scientific prediction?** Yes.
330	- **C1 / P2:** the likely verdict moves from UNDETERMINED to NON-CONFORMS, if R-73..R-76 are obtained and do not show the proviso met.
331	- **C1 bearing:** changes as in D6. It no longer requires that nothing responded before R-87.
332	- **G-D1 applies.** If the absence of a permitting text before 16:10 relies on R-81..R-85 having had no force until R-86 adopted them, the result is DISJUNCTIVE {H-D status clause, H-B conformance}.
333	
334	**(5) Frozen rule.**
335	> **FR-D9.**
336	> - **P** = R-72's RED condition and proviso ("no unresolved governance blockers"; the named ARB decisions and scope ruling have landed) are shown met by texts in force before 16:10.
337	> - **B** = a text in force before 16:10 blocks WP-4B, read by default as covering all WP-4B work including producer-agnostic RED, and no text in force before 16:10 narrows that scope to exclude RED.
338	>
339	> Verdicts:
340	> - **CONFORMS** iff P ∧ ¬B.
341	> - **NON-CONFORMS** iff the required texts (R-72 to R-80) were obtained and ¬(P ∧ ¬B).
342	> - **UNDETERMINED** iff a required text could not be obtained, or the entry-into-force time of a text that decides P or B is NOT_IDENTIFIABLE relative to 16:10.
343	>
344	> Entry into force: an adoption form, if the ruling is status-mediated; otherwise, not earlier than its recording time. Stated dates are SOURCE_STATED.
345	>
346	> The 16:10 time of R11 is itself a git date (SOURCE_STATED). The verdict carries that label.
347	
348	---
349	
350	## D10: the P1 census and the P8 tendency are under-specified
351	
352	**(1) Defect, quoted.**
353	> "The P1-HB census refutes only **H-B restricted to window W**, and the spec does not say so. Reading H-B's clause as existential is also an interpretive choice that is not labelled UNKNOWN. Under the other reading ('when the work condition is met, the state changes'), one clean counter-instance would be enough. The P8 'tendency ⇒ census' option gives no threshold, so it cannot be tested."
354	
355	**(2) Correction.**
356	- **P1-HB:** label the quantifier reading UNKNOWN, and test both readings:
357	  - **Reading 1a (existential):** the census over W. A negative result is stated as "H-B reading 1a is not instantiated in W". It is never stated as "H-B refuted".
358	  - **Reading 1b (conditional-universal):** one eligible target whose work condition is met, and whose state is unchanged by NIF until a separate act, refutes 1b.
359	- **P8:** drop the tendency reading. No source gives a threshold, and inventing one would be arbitrary. P8 is tested as a universal. If H-B's authors intend a tendency, P8 is declared NOT_TESTABLE_AS_SPECIFIED and is not scored.
360	
361	**(3) Why this is sufficient.**
362	- The logical force of each test now matches its quantifier:
363	  - An existential claim is refuted only by exhausting its domain, so the conclusion is limited to the exhausted domain W.
364	  - A conditional-universal claim is refuted by one instance.
365	- Reporting both readings keeps the interpretation from being decided after the fact.
366	- Dropping the tendency reading removes the only untestable option. Keeping it without a threshold would have left P8 unfalsifiable.
367	
368	**(4) Does it change a scientific prediction?** Yes.
369	- **P1-HB:** the conclusion is scoped to W, and a second, stronger test (1b) is added.
370	- **P8-HB:** only the universal reading remains.
371	
372	**(5) Frozen rule.**
373	> **FR-D10.** P1-HB is scored under both readings.
374	> - 1a: "not instantiated in W" or "instantiated".
375	> - 1b: FIRED if at least one eligible counter-instance is found (with NIF).
376	>
377	> Neither result is generalized beyond W. P8 is universal only. The tendency reading is NOT_TESTABLE_AS_SPECIFIED.
378	
379	---
380	
381	## D11: attestation fields assume artefacts that no input establishes
382	
383	**(1) Defect, quoted.**
384	> "The feasibility section is hedged, but the **attestation fields assume** artefacts that no input establishes: CI runs with CI start times; 'server push time' (git history does not record it); 'adopted' R-86 and R-90 (R-90 appears in the inputs in a withdrawal context); adoption records for R-77, R-79 and R-80; 'DA session logs'; version control of IMPLEMENTATION_PROGRESS.md; a register kept as a git file. STATE lists only a register, a few session logs and **one** commit."
385	
386	**(2) Correction.**
387	- Phrase every such field as "if such an artefact exists".
388	- Give a fallback for each, with its grade, in the table in §0.11.
389	- Mark R-90's status as UNKNOWN.
390	- Note that git dates (including R11's 16:10) are client-set (§0.9).
391	
392	**(3) Why this is sufficient.**
393	- The defect is an existence assumption hidden inside field definitions.
394	- After the correction, every field is defined whether or not its preferred artefact exists: either the fallback applies with a stated grade, or the field is UNDETERMINED.
395	- So no result can depend silently on an artefact that no input shows exists.
396	
397	**(4) Does it change a scientific prediction?** No. Some outcomes are downgraded, for example to FIRED-CONDITIONAL or UNDETERMINED, when the preferred artefacts do not exist.
398	
399	**(5) Frozen rule.**
400	> **FR-D11.** Every attestation names a preferred artefact "if it exists", a fallback, and the grade of the fallback (§0.11). A field whose preferred and fallback sources are both missing is UNDETERMINED. The capture reports which artefacts exist.
401	
402	---
403	
404	## D12: P7-HD depends on motive; P8-HD repeats P1
405	
406	**(1) Defect, quoted.**
407	> "P7's H-D falsifier ('treated as authorized **because** the predecessor was accepted') depends on motive and cannot be observed as behaviour. It also cannot fire in the R-89 episode, because an authorizing act (R-89) exists. P8's H-D falsifier just repeats P1."
408	
409	**(2) Correction.**
410	- **P7-HD:** NOT_APPLICABLE to the R-89 episode.
411	- **P7-HD in other episodes:** restated in behavioural and NIF terms. NIF shows the successor authorized and in force, and no norm-making act in a complete DCS produced that authorization. This *is* P1 on the gate, and it is scored under P1 only.
412	- **P8-HD:** points to P1 and is not scored separately.
413	
414	**(3) Why this is sufficient.**
415	- The motive clause ("because") is removed, so every remaining condition is observable.
416	- In the R-89 episode, the premise "no authorizing act" is false by construction, since R-89 exists as a text. So declaring the limb NOT_APPLICABLE is exact.
417	- Scoring P7-HD and P8-HD under P1 only removes the double counting.
418	
419	**(4) Does it change a scientific prediction?** Yes.
420	- **P7-HD:** it is dropped for the R-89 episode, and elsewhere merged into P1.
421	- **P8-HD:** it is merged into P1.
422	- H-D's operational predictions are therefore tested only through P1, P4 and P5.
423	
424	**(5) Frozen rule.**
425	> **FR-D12.** P7-HD is NOT_APPLICABLE when any norm-making act authorizing the successor exists in the DCS, whatever that act's status. Otherwise, P7-HD and P8-HD are instances of P1-HD and are scored only there.
426	
427	---
428	
429	## D13: the status-mediation upgrade is only partial
430	
431	**(1) Defect, quoted.**
432	> "Item 1 (an adoption entry written by the adopter) is still the norm-maker's own act; only its system time and authenticated identity are independent. The behavioural contrast (item 3) is empty unless work was ready and waiting during the prepared interval. As written, the upgrade moves status mediation only **part of the way** to independent observation."
433	
434	**(2) Correction.** (§3)
435	- **Item 1:** relabelled as the norm-maker's own act. Only its recording time and its AUTH_ID are independent (FR-D7).
436	- **New item 0:** NIF-A for status, if Part C finds such a channel.
437	- **Item 2:** uptake is restricted to NIF-B (third-party application). NIF-C is recorded only.
438	- **Item 3:** the contrast gets an **eligibility condition**. During the prepared interval, a work item that depends on the ruling was *pending*: its preconditions were met, and it was queued or planned, attested by an artefact with a system-recorded time. A contrast without such an item is VACUOUS and is not scored.
439	- **Absence of work** in the prepared interval requires a complete execution channel (FR-D5e).
440	
441	**(3) Why this is sufficient.**
442	- The upgrade was partial on two counts:
443	  - Its first item was not independent. The correction now claims only what is independent (time and identity), and it adds the only fully independent source (NIF-A).
444	  - Its contrast could be vacuous. The eligibility condition ensures that "no execution during the prepared interval" is informative: work was ready, so its absence is a behavioural difference and not a lack of opportunity.
445	
446	**(4) Does it change a scientific prediction?** Yes, for H-D's status clause (P4). An observed contrast now counts only if it is eligible. H-B's predictions are not affected, because H-B is silent here (SOURCE FACT: IDENTIFIABILITY P4).
447	
448	**(5) Frozen rule.**
449	> **FR-D13.** Status mediation counts as independently observed only if:
450	> - (0) NIF-A records the status transition, **or**
451	> - (1) an adoption form has a recording time and AUTH_ID, **and** (2) NIF-B uptake follows adoption, **and** (3) an **eligible** contrast is present: pending dependent work existed during the prepared interval, and a complete execution channel shows no execution on it and no NIF-B application before adoption.
452	>
453	> Otherwise, status mediation stays SELF_REPORTED or PARTIALLY_INDEPENDENT.
454	
455	---
456	
457	## D14: labels and optional items
458	
459	**(1) Defect, quoted.**
460	> "The ranking is labelled INFERENCE but is a judgement (PROPOSAL). The R-86 'waiting' quote is a SOURCE FACT; reading it as a behavioural instance is INFERENCE. P4 lists R-88's text, which only orders the rulings and says nothing about force. P7's GREEN/VERIFY CI run serves C2's evidence limb, not the gate falsifier. The 'input conflict' may be only apparent: '§WP-4 remains OPEN' may refer to WP-4 as a whole, not WP-4B, and C2's textual order does not establish the order of entry into force."
461	
462	**(2) Correction.**
463	- **Ranking:** relabelled PROPOSAL.
464	- **R-86 "waiting":** the quote is SOURCE FACT; reading it as a behavioural instance is INFERENCE.
465	- **R-88 text:** OPTIONAL.
466	- **GREEN/VERIFY run:** OPTIONAL, and serves C2's evidence limb only.
467	- **Input conflict:** restated as "possibly only apparent", for two reasons. "§WP-4 remains OPEN" may refer to WP-4 as a whole. And C2 orders texts, which is SOURCE_STATED_ORDER of drafting, not an order of entry into force.
468	
469	**(3) Why this is sufficient.** Each item is a mislabel or a wrongly required field. Relabelling or marking a field OPTIONAL fixes each one completely, and none of them is a premise of a falsifier.
470	
471	**(4) Does it change a scientific prediction?** No.
472	
473	**(5) Frozen rule.**
474	> **FR-D14.** Judgements are labelled PROPOSAL. Readings of quotes are labelled INFERENCE. Fields that are not premises of any falsifier are marked OPTIONAL. Textual order is labelled SOURCE_STATED_ORDER, and it never establishes the order of entry into force.
475	
476	---
477	
478	# PART A (continued). The complete corrected specification 1bb-r1
479	
480	## §0. Scope and shared rules
481	
482	### §0.1 Scope [UNCHANGED]
483	- **SOURCE FACT:** No prediction is identified on the current corpus (IDENTIFIABILITY `identified: []`).
484	- **PROPOSAL:** A prediction is in scope if some observation puts one hypothesis at risk while the other survives it. In scope: **P1** (only under H-B reading 1), **P2, P4, P5, P7, P8**. Excluded:
485	  - **P3**: act-mediated feedback fits both hypotheses, and its act-less part is P1.
486	  - **P6**: both hypotheses are met at every record boundary.
487	- **[NEW D1]** Being in scope is necessary but not sufficient. Each prediction's discrimination status also depends on NIF availability (§1.7).
488	
489	### §0.2 Labels [UNCHANGED, extended]
490	- SOURCE FACT, INFERENCE, PROPOSAL and UNKNOWN, as in 1bb.
491	- **[NEW D1, D5, D11]** Grades, order labels and categories are defined in §0.3, §0.4 and §0.9.
492	
493	### §0.3 The six distinctions [NEW D1; HUMAN-DECISIONS]
494	These categories are recorded separately for every episode. None is inferred from another, except by the rules stated here.
495	
496	| Code | Distinction | What can establish it | What can never establish it |
497	|---|---|---|---|
498	| **N-EXISTS** | The norm exists: a text of the norm is recorded (including PREPARED texts). | The record's text. Its time is a recording time (§0.9). | — |
499	| **N-FORCE** | The norm is in force at t. | NIF-A, or NIF-B (labelled N-FORCE[OPERATIONAL]). The graded fallback (§0.4) gives at most FIRED-CONDITIONAL. | The ruling's self-assertion; statements by the maker; recording time; executor behaviour; N-EXISTS alone. |
500	| **N-KNOWN** | The norm is known, or claimed, to be in force by actor X. | X's statement: NIF-C if X is a third party; MAKER_FORCE_ASSERTION if X is the maker; SELF_ASSERTION if the statement is inside the ruling. | It never establishes N-FORCE. |
501	| **ACT-CONF** | An act according to the norm: an execution at t whose operation is permitted by the norms in force at t⁻. | An execution trace plus N-FORCE of a permitting norm at t⁻. | An execution trace alone. |
502	| **ACT-CONTRA** | An act contrary to the norm: an execution at t whose operation is not permitted at t⁻. | An execution trace plus N-FORCE of a prohibiting norm at t⁻, or the absence of any permitting norm in force at t⁻ (which requires a complete DCS, §0.8). | An execution trace alone. |
503	| **N-CHANGE-NOACT** | The norm changes without a norm-making act. | N-FORCE at t1 ≠ N-FORCE at t2, both by NIF; plus a complete DCS showing no norm-making act in [t1,t2], no prior conditional act producing the change, and no late-recorded act claiming effect in [t1,t2]. | A work event alone (HUMAN-DECISIONS). A ruling asserting its own adoption. |
504	
505	### §0.4 Independent observables of the norm in force (NIF) and rule G-D1 [NEW D1]
506	- **NIF-A (independent norm-status record).** An entry in a channel that meets independence criteria I1–I4 (Part C §C.4) and records the *normative state* of the norm (in force or not in force) at t, with a system-generated time. Its availability is determined by Part C.
507	- **NIF-B (third-party application).** An act by an actor who is not the maker or adopter of the norm and not the executor of the work under test. The act applies the norm as binding: it grants, refuses, accepts or blocks on the norm's basis. It must carry AUTH_ID and a recording time.
508	  - It establishes N-FORCE[OPERATIONAL]. This is a PROPOSAL: application produces normative consequences, which are observable effects of force; citation does not.
509	  - If the application is later expressly voided as erroneous, its grade drops to FIRED-CONDITIONAL.
510	- **NIF-C (third-party citation).** A statement by such an actor that the norm governs, without applying it. It establishes N-KNOWN only. It is recorded, and it never fires a falsifier.
511	- **Not NIF:**
512	  - the executor's work under the norm (ACT);
513	  - the ruling's self-assertion ("effective immediately");
514	  - statements by the maker or adopter ("R-89 already governs authorization");
515	  - register recording times.
516	- **Graded fallback (maker's records).** This fallback is allowed only where §1.7 permits it. A premise about force may be taken from the norm-maker's records (text, adoption forms, recording times) in a DCS shown complete (§0.8). A falsifier built on such a premise is at most **FIRED-CONDITIONAL**, with the condition "the maker's records state force accurately".
517	- **G-D1.** If a premise "N (not) in force at t" is established only by (a) executor behaviour or (b) applying H-D's status rule (force only through adoption) to the maker's records, then every falsifier that uses it is graded **DISJUNCTIVE {H-D clause, H-B clause}**. This means "at least one fails; which one is not identified".
518	
519	### §0.5 Attestation rule [CHANGED D7]
520	1B's three conditions are kept, and their scope is corrected.
521	- **Observation versus attestation.** A record R of an act is the observation of that act. R may attest only two things about itself:
522	  - its writer identity, graded AUTH_ID or ACTOR_SET_ID;
523	  - its recording time, graded by §0.9.
524	
525	  R never attests its stated effective date or the norm's force.
526	- A field of any other observation is **independently attested** only if its attesting artefact:
527	  1. has a writer different from the maker, the adopter and the executor **[UNCHANGED in substance]**;
528	  2. does not copy the ruling's self-statements. Artefacts that *cite* the ruling are admissible as *observations* of uptake (NIF-B, NIF-C, ACT) **[CHANGED D7]**;
529	  3. carries a system-generated timestamp. A committer or author date is client-set, and is SOURCE_STATED (§0.9) **[CHANGED D11]**.
530	- Anything a ruling says about itself is self-report: "effective immediately", "R-89 already governs" **[UNCHANGED]**.
531	- **SOURCE FACT:** recording time ≠ decision time ≠ entry into force **[UNCHANGED]**. **[CHANGED D5, D9]** Entry into force comes from an adoption form (AF-1 to AF-3) when the ruling is status-mediated. Otherwise it is "not earlier than its recording time". It never comes from the time a row was recorded, taken as a decision time.
532	
533	### §0.6 Declared channel set and capability register [CHANGED D5]
534	- **Capability register v0** **[CHANGED D5(f)]**. This is frozen before acquisition, not before reading: R-86 and R-90 have been read through the inputs.
535	  - **SOURCE FACT:** R-86 names the Decision Authority (DA) as the only adopter.
536	  - **SOURCE FACT (STATE):** Chief-prepared rulings gain force when the DA adopts them.
537	  - **UNKNOWN:** who is capable of making operational dispositions (R-94 type). The operational/constitutional split is known only through IDENTIFIABILITY's reading of R-90, which appears in a withdrawal context. It is resolved only by R-90's text and status in Stage 1. If it remains unresolved, P5 is NON-DISCRIMINATING.
538	- **Declared channel set (DCS) for norm-making acts, v0** **[CHANGED D5(a)]**:
539	  - **K-REG**: the register of rulings, and its write history if it is versioned.
540	  - **K-SESS**: session logs (S0804, S0815, and later ones).
541	  - **K-PROG**: IMPLEMENTATION_PROGRESS.md, which holds Chief dispositions and execution reports.
542	
543	  DCS v1 = DCS v0 plus any channel for which Part C returns Q1 = YES and Q2 ∋ {ADOPTION_EVENT, APPROVAL_EVENT, NORM_STATE}. DCS v1 is closed before Stage 1.
544	- **"No act"** means "no norm-making act in DCS v1 in the window, with DCS v1 shown complete (§0.8)". It never means proving that no unrecorded act happened anywhere **[UNCHANGED in intent]**.
545	- **OUT_OF_CHANNEL_ACT** **[NEW D5(a)]**: a norm-making act found outside DCS v1. It shows that DCS v1 is incomplete for that target, and it makes the "no act" premise UNDETERMINED. It is never scored as N-CHANGE-NOACT.
546	- **Late recording** **[NEW D5(b)]**: see §0.9.
547	- **Adoption forms** **[NEW D5(c)]**. This list is exhaustive.
548	  - **AF-1**: the status annotation of the ruling row changes to ADOPTED (or "adopted"), written under the DA's identity.
549	  - **AF-2**: a separate entry by the DA that names the ruling id or ids and contains an adoption performative ("adopt", "adopted", "hereby adopts").
550	  - **AF-3**: a DA ruling that declares named prepared rulings governing, in performative form. This is the R-86 pattern: "These become governing rulings effective immediately".
551	  - **Not an adoption:** a descriptive assertion by the maker that force already exists, such as "R-89 already governs authorization". This is MAKER_FORCE_ASSERTION.
552	  - **Sensitivity:** the outcome under the opposite classification is reported, but never scored.
553	- **Identity** **[NEW D5(d)]**:
554	  - **AUTH_ID**: a signature verified against a key list fixed before Stage 1, or an account-bound record on the hosting server (an approval, merge or audit event).
555	  - **ACTOR_SET_ID**: git author or committer fields, and names in text.
556	
557	  If an identity-dependent premise has only ACTOR_SET_ID, the grade is at most FIRED-CONDITIONAL.
558	
559	### §0.7 Execution-channel register [NEW D5(e)]
560	- **Execution channel EC v0:**
561	  - the git repository or repositories named by the human before Part B runs (Part B §1);
562	  - CI run records, if Part C finds that they exist.
563	- An **execution trace** is defined in Part B §3.
564	- An **absence of work** on target X is admissible only if EC is shown complete for X (§0.8). Otherwise it is NOT-EVIDENCED-IN-CAPTURE.
565	
566	### §0.8 Absence and completeness [NEW D2, D5]
567	An absence claim ("no act", "no adoption", "no waiver", "no work", "no response") counts as a falsifier premise only if the channel is shown complete over the window. That requires all four of the following:
568	1. **Coverage:** the channel is *required* for that kind of event, by a rule in force over the window, shown by NIF-A or by configuration enforced by the host (Part C Q6).
569	2. **Capture:** the capture is not shallow or partial, and its refs equal the server's refs at capture time.
570	3. **Retention:** records covering the window are retained.
571	4. **Integrity:** there is no undetected deletion or rewrite in the window, shown by an audit log or by tamper-evidence.
572	
573	Otherwise the absence is **NOT-EVIDENCED-IN-CAPTURE**, and a falsifier that needs it is **UNDETERMINED**.

# SPEC 1bb-r1: corrected specification, plus two frozen search protocols

**Status.** This is a specification only. **Nothing has been collected.** No command in this document has been run. Every command in Parts B and C is written to be run later, verbatim, by a worker, and then checked by a reviewer.

**Inputs used (only these):** `SPEC-1bb.md`, `SPEC-1bb.json`, `REVIEW-1bb.md` (defects D1–D14), `HYPOTHESES.md`, `IDENTIFIABILITY.json`, `CONFORMANCE-CASE.json`, `STATE.md`, `HUMAN-DECISIONS.md`.

**Labels** (kept from 1bb): SOURCE FACT (stated in an input file), INFERENCE (derived from inputs), PROPOSAL (a specification choice), UNKNOWN.

**Change marks** used in the corrected specification:

# PART A. Defect-by-defect correction (D1–D14)

For each defect, this part gives: (1) the defect, quoted from REVIEW-1bb; (2) the correction; (3) why the correction is logically sufficient; (4) whether it changes a scientific prediction, and which one; (5) the corrected rule, stated so it can be frozen.

A distinction used throughout item (4):
- The **hypothesis-level claims** are the clauses of H-D and H-B in HYPOTHESES.md. They are frozen, and no correction changes them.
- The **operational prediction** is the observation this spec says each clause predicts, together with its falsifier. Corrections can change this.

## D1: the same observation serves both sides

**(1) Defect, quoted.**
> "**The same observation serves both sides.** 'R-89 not adopted, but work ran under it' is read as H-D's status clause failing. But the spec's own P2 and P7 falsifiers read the same observation as **non-conformance**: execution under an act that is not in force, before WP-4B's acceptance and with no waiver. That falsifies H-B. H-D can say 'R-89 had no force; engineering broke the norm'. H-B can say 'work changed the norm'. Behavioural uptake cannot tell *the norm changed without an act* from *work violated an unchanged norm*. The same confound affects P5's 'not in force' branch and P1's H-D falsifier, which requires only that the after-state is 'acted on by engineering'."

**(2) Correction.**
- Introduce the **six distinctions** of HUMAN-DECISIONS.md as separate recorded categories (§0.3).
- Introduce an **independent observable of the norm in force** (NIF, §0.4), in three tiers:
  - **NIF-A**: an independent norm-status record.
  - **NIF-B**: application of the norm as binding by a third party, meaning an actor who is not the maker or adopter of that norm and not the executor of the work under test.
  - **NIF-C**: a statement by such a third party that the norm governs.
- Work by the executor is **never** a NIF. It is recorded only as an act, either according to the norm or contrary to it.
- Add the generic rule **G-D1** (§0.4). If a falsifier premise about the norm in force is established only through (a) executor behaviour or (b) applying H-D's status rule to the norm-maker's own records, the result is recorded as **DISJUNCTIVE**: "at least one of {clause X of H-D, clause Y of H-B} fails; which one is not identified". It is not recorded as a falsification of either hypothesis.
- For **each** prediction, state which NIF is required. Without that NIF, declare the prediction NON-DISCRIMINATING, DISJUNCTIVE or UNDETERMINED (§1.7).
- Split the headline test into two limbs with disjoint observables:
  - **H-D force limb:** NIF-A or NIF-B shows the norm in force while no adoption form exists.
  - **H-B conformance limb:** an execution trace, plus a NIF (or the graded fallback) showing that the operation was not permitted at t⁻.
- This narrows the reviewer's fix in one respect. The reviewer proposed "citation as governing by a non-adopting, non-executing actor" as the H-D force test. A citation shows only that the norm is *known (believed) to be in force* (distinction 3), which HUMAN-DECISIONS.md requires to be kept apart from *in force* (distinction 2). So bare citation is tier NIF-C: it is recorded but cannot fire a falsifier. Only **application** by such an actor (NIF-B) or an independent status record (NIF-A) can.

**(3) Why this is sufficient.**
- D1 is a failure of identification: one observation O (work under R-89 while R-89 is not adopted) is predicted by the conjunction "H-D status clause holds, and H-B conformance fails", and also by "H-D status clause fails, and H-B conformance holds". So O cannot separate them.
- After the correction, each limb rests on an observable the other limb does not use:
  - The H-D limb uses NIF-A or NIF-B about R-89's force. Neither is an act of the executor, so H-B's conformance clause says nothing about it.
  - The H-B limb uses the norm in force at t⁻ established by NIF (or the graded fallback). It does not use H-D's status rule, because G-D1 downgrades any premise that does.
- The executor's behaviour enters only as distinction 4 or 5 (an act according to or contrary to a norm), never as distinction 2 (the norm in force) or 6 (a norm change without an act). So no single observation can be counted for both sides.
- When only O is available, G-D1 records the result as DISJUNCTIVE. That is the strongest conclusion that follows logically: O is incompatible with "both clauses hold" (given no waiver in force), but it does not say which clause fails.

**(4) Does it change a scientific prediction?** Yes, at the operational level. The hypothesis-level claims are unchanged.
- **P4 H-D falsifier:** "work executed citing R-89" no longer counts. It now requires NIF-A or NIF-B.
- **P1 H-D falsifier:** the after-state must be established by NIF. "Acted on by engineering" no longer suffices.
- **P5:** the "effective" branch and the "not in force" branch both require NIF. Otherwise the result is DISJUNCTIVE.
- **P2 and P7 H-B falsifiers:** if the non-permission premise rests on the status rule (for example, "R-81..R-85 governed only via R-86", or "R-87 was not yet adopted"), the result becomes DISJUNCTIVE.
- **§5, branch 1:** changed from "H-D's status clause falsified" to DISJUNCTIVE, unless NIF is present.

**(5) Frozen rule.**
> **FR-D1.** An observation made only of executor behaviour establishes, at most, an act according to or contrary to a norm (distinctions 4 and 5). It never establishes a norm being in force (distinction 2) or a norm change without an act (distinction 6).
>
> A premise "norm N is (not) in force at t" counts toward a falsifier only if it is established by NIF-A or NIF-B. NIF-C, statements by the maker, a ruling's self-assertion and recording times never count.
>
> **G-D1.** If a premise about force is established only by (a) executor behaviour or (b) applying H-D's status rule (force comes only from adoption) to the maker's records, then any falsifier that uses the premise is graded **DISJUNCTIVE {H-D clause, H-B clause}**.
>
> Each prediction carries the NIF requirement listed in §1.7. Without it, the prediction is scored NON-DISCRIMINATING or DISJUNCTIVE, as listed there.

## D2: the three items are not sufficient

**(1) Defect, quoted.**
> "**The three items are not sufficient.** The spec's own P4 and P7 falsifiers also need: (a) a link showing that the WP-4C-1 work was done under R-89 or cites it; (b) the closed-channel history of waivers and responses up to WP-4C-1's acceptance; (c) R-72's gate being in force at t_first_work; (d) citations by non-adopting actors. Also, 'no adoption up to 2026-08-15' needs the **whole** write history over the window, so 'about 3 records' understates the effort. The outcome list also leaves out **'no WP-4C-1 work by 2026-08-15'**. That outcome is plausible for a PREPARED, NOT ADOPTED ruling, and in it neither falsifier can fire, so the acquisition discriminates nothing."

**(2) Correction.** Replace the three-item acquisition with a **two-stage acquisition** (§5).
- **Stage 0** has two parts:
  - the rank-0 WP-4C-1 check (Part B);
  - the norm-status-channel scoping search (Part C).
- **Stage 1** runs only if Stage 0 finds an execution trace. It adds items (a)–(d):
  - (a) the link from the work to R-89;
  - (b) the full write history of the declared channels over the P7 window, covering adoption, waiver and response entries;
  - (c) R-72's gate being in force at t_w;
  - (d) NIF-B applications and NIF-C citations by third parties.

  It also adds R-89's text, to test whether R-89 itself waives or supersedes the gate.
- The effort is restated. The whole write history over the window is required, so this is not "about 3 records".
- Freeze an **outcome table** (O0–O8) that includes **O0: no WP-4C-1 execution trace in the capture**, before anything is acquired.

**(3) Why this is sufficient.**
- Each falsifier that §5 relies on (P4-HD, P7-HB) now has every premise mapped to an acquisition item:
  - "work under R-89" maps to (a);
  - "no adoption" and "no waiver" map to (b), together with the completeness rule in §0.8;
  - "gate in force" maps to (c);
  - "force without adoption" maps to (d), or to NIF-A from Part C.
- The outcome table is exhaustive over the branches: trace present or absent; R-89 adopted, not adopted, or not identifiable; NIF present or absent; acceptance before or after the work.
- Because O0 is explicit, the case where the acquisition discriminates nothing is known in advance, and the ranking is made conditional on it (D3).

**(4) Does it change a scientific prediction?** No. It changes the acquisition, its effort estimate and the outcome table. The newly listed outcome O0 predicts nothing for either hypothesis.

**(5) Frozen rule.**
> **FR-D2.** The smallest acquisition is two-stage.
> - Stage 0 = Part B and Part C, both run before any Stage 1 item.
> - Stage 1 runs only if Stage 0 returns at least one execution trace (ET-1 or ET-2). It acquires items S1-a to S1-g (§5).
>
> Outcomes are scored only against table O0–O8 (§5), which is frozen now. O0 ("NOT-EVIDENCED-IN-CAPTURE" or "CAPTURE_INVALID") means that P4 and P7 discriminate nothing, and P2 moves to rank 1.

## D4: windows start at recording times

**(1) Defect, quoted.**
> "The P7 window starts at **R-89's recording time**. WP-4C-1 work that began *before* R-89 was recorded is the strongest possible case against H-B, and this window excludes it. P4 and P5 also start at recording times, although STATE says recording time ≠ decision time ≠ entry into force. The §5 item 'first WP-4C-1 commit' has no window at all."

**(2) Correction.**
- **P7:** the window starts at the earlier of (i) the earliest recorded trace of R-72 and (ii) the earliest WP-4C-1 execution trace. It ends at the earlier of WP-4C-1's acceptance entering force and 2026-08-15.
- **P4 and P5:** the window starts at the earliest recorded trace of the ruling in **any** declared channel, not at its register row.
- **Rank-0 check:** it has **no lower bound** at all (Part B §6), so the "earliest WP-4C-1 artefact" is found and not assumed.
- **§5:** item "first WP-4C-1 commit" gets its window from Part B.

**(3) Why this is sufficient.**
- The defect is that the window excludes admissible falsifying cases. The new P7 start is ≤ every time at which a WP-4C-1 trace could exist in the capture, because it takes the minimum with the earliest trace, and the rank-0 search that finds that trace has no lower bound. So no WP-4C-1 execution in the capture can fall before the window.
- For P4 and P5, "earliest recorded trace in any declared channel" is ≤ the register row's time by construction. So no earlier trace is excluded.
- The windows still use recording times, because no earlier time is observable. But they use them only as lower bounds on existence, never as decision times or times of entry into force (§0.9).

**(4) Does it change a scientific prediction?** Yes.
- **P7 H-B falsifier:** it can now be fired by WP-4C-1 work that began before R-89 was recorded, and even before R-72's earliest trace. In that case the relevant norm is "no authorization", not R-72's gate.
- **P4 and P5:** earlier traces are brought into scope. The falsifier conditions themselves are unchanged.

**(5) Frozen rule.**
> **FR-D4.** Every window starts at the earliest recorded trace of the relevant object in the declared channel set, or earlier. The rank-0 search has no lower bound.
> - P7 window = [min(earliest trace of R-72, earliest WP-4C-1 ET), min(WP-4C-1 acceptance in force, 2026-08-15)].
> - P4 window = [earliest trace of R-89, min(first adoption or withdrawal form, 2026-08-15)].
> - P5 window = [earliest trace of R-94, attested execution], followed by the P8 window.
>
> A recording time is used only as a bound on existence.

## D5: the closed-world register is not well defined

**(1) Defect, quoted.**
> "**Not well defined.** (a) R-86 names the *adopter*; the *single channel* is the spec's own assumption. The Chief's operational dispositions (R-94, and R-90's operational/constitutional split) and the DA's 'R-89 already governs' may sit in other channels, such as session logs or progress files. An act made there would show up as an 'act-less change'. (b) **Late recording:** an act decided in the window but recorded afterwards looks like 'no entry in window'. The spec has no rule for this, although recording ≠ decision is a SOURCE FACT. (c) There is no rule, fixed in advance, for **what form counts as an adoption**. The spec says the DA's statement 'may itself be the adoption' and leaves it there, so the outcome can be decided after the fact. (d) Actor identity rests on git author/committer names, which the actor sets. (e) There is **no closed world for work**, yet P1-HB ('executed nothing'), P7 ('first work event') and the status-mediation contrast ('no execution') all need an absence of work. (f) 'Fixed before looking at the data' is impossible: R-86 and R-90 have already been read."

**(2) Correction.** One fix for each sub-defect (§0.6 and §0.7).
- **(a)** A **declared channel set** for norm-making acts, v0, is frozen now:
  - the register;
  - session logs;
  - IMPLEMENTATION_PROGRESS.md;
  - any hosting-server approval channel that Part C finds.

  It is closed once more, by Part C's output, before Stage 1. An act found outside the set is labelled OUT_OF_CHANNEL_ACT. Such a find makes the "no act" premise UNDETERMINED. It never makes it a falsification.
- **(b) Late recording.** Acts are placed by their recording time only for RECORDING_ORDER. If an act is recorded after the window but states an effect inside the window, then both "no act in the window" and "act in force in the window" become NOT_IDENTIFIABLE for that target, and the falsifiers that use them are UNDETERMINED.
- **(c) Adoption forms.** The forms AF-1, AF-2 and AF-3 are frozen as an exhaustive list. Descriptive statements by the maker that force already exists ("R-89 already governs") are MAKER_FORCE_ASSERTION, **not** adoption. A sensitivity result under the opposite reading is reported but never scored.
- **(d) Identity.** AUTH_ID means a verified signature against a key list fixed before Stage 1, or an account record on the hosting server. ACTOR_SET_ID means git name and email fields, and names in text. A premise that rests on ACTOR_SET_ID caps the grade at FIRED-CONDITIONAL.
- **(e) Work.** Add an **execution-channel register** (§0.7). A premise of *absence of work* is admissible only if the execution channel is shown complete (§0.8). Otherwise it is NOT-EVIDENCED-IN-CAPTURE.
- **(f) Timing of freezing.** "Fixed before looking at the data" is replaced by "fixed before acquiring any new evidence (Stage 0 or Stage 1)". The capability register v0 is stated openly to rest on texts that have already been read (R-86 as quoted in the inputs), so it is not blind. The capability for operational dispositions is UNKNOWN, and it is not settled by choice.

**(3) Why this is sufficient.**
- Each sub-defect is a way the "no act" or "no work" premise could come out true when an act or work in fact existed, or be decided after the fact. Each fix blocks that path:
  - (a) An act outside the assumed channel can no longer produce a false act-less change, because finding it blocks the premise, and not finding it counts as absence only within a declared, closed set.
  - (b) A late-recorded act can no longer produce a false act-less change or a false "waiver in force". Its effect time is NOT_IDENTIFIABLE, which blocks both.
  - (c) The adoption verdict is fixed by a rule stated now, so it cannot be chosen after seeing the outcome.
  - (d) An identity set by the actor can no longer support a clean result.
  - (e) An absence of work now needs a demonstrated complete channel, as an absence of acts does.
  - (f) The claim that cannot be met is replaced by one that can be verified (the freeze precedes acquisition), and the residual non-blindness is disclosed.
- None of these fixes removes a falsifier. They only add the premises the falsifiers already needed.

**(4) Does it change a scientific prediction?** Yes, at the operational level.
- **P1-HD, P4-HD and P5-HD** ("no act" or "no adoption"): each now needs a complete declared channel set and the adoption-form rule. A late-recorded act gives UNDETERMINED.
- **P1-HB, P7-HB and the status-mediation contrast** ("no work" premises): each now needs execution-channel completeness.
- **R-89:** under the frozen form rule, the DA's "already governs" is not an adoption. So if no AF-1, AF-2 or AF-3 exists, R-89 counts as not adopted.

**(5) Frozen rule.**
> **FR-D5.**
> - (a) Norm-making acts are sought only in the declared channel set DCS. DCS v0 = {K-REG, K-SESS, K-PROG}. It is extended only by Part C's result, and it is closed before Stage 1. An act found outside DCS is labelled OUT_OF_CHANNEL_ACT, and the "no act" premise for that target becomes UNDETERMINED.
> - (b) An act placed after the window by recording time, but claiming an effect inside the window, makes the relevant premises NOT_IDENTIFIABLE.
> - (c) Adoption = AF-1, AF-2 or AF-3 (§0.6) and nothing else.
> - (d) Premises that rest on identity require AUTH_ID for a clean grade. With ACTOR_SET_ID only, the grade is at most FIRED-CONDITIONAL.
> - (e) Absence of work requires a complete execution channel (§0.7, §0.8).
> - (f) All rules are frozen before any Stage 0 command runs. Non-blindness toward R-86 and R-90 is disclosed.

## D6: P2 adds a response requirement

**(1) Defect, quoted.**
> "HYPOTHESES says only that work 'is expected to **conform**'. The spec's P2 claim adds that 'the system responds (sanction, remediation or waiver) before acceptance'. That makes H-B harder to falsify, overlaps P8, and makes C1's bearing depend on R-87. The window end ('acceptance takes force') is not justified. A later execution-governance repair (R-91 deviation → R-94 Constitutional Review, listed by the spec under P8) might be a response to R11, and this window would ignore it."

**(2) Correction.**
- **P2 claim:** reduced to conformance as stated. Every execution event occurs when the norm in force at t_exec⁻ permits the operation. The falsifier is one clean non-permitted execution with no waiver in force *ex ante*.
- **Response** (sanction, remediation, or a retroactive waiver) is moved to **P8**, where non-conformance counts as a deviation. P8 has its own window (from the deviation to the next execution on the same target). Late responses are recorded as LATE_RESPONSE, whenever they occur.
- A retroactive waiver does not turn a non-conforming execution into a conforming one. It is a response.
- Stage 1 checks whether R-91 or R-94 refer to R11.
- The **C1 bearing** no longer depends on R-87.
- The same change applies to **P7-HB**, which had the same response clause.

**(3) Why this is sufficient.**
- The defect is that P2 tested the conjunction "conformance, or else a timely response", which H-B does not state. Removing the disjunct makes the tested clause equal to the stated one ("expected to conform").
- The response clause is still tested, as H-B's feedback clause (P8), so no part of H-B is left untested.
- The arbitrary window end disappears with the clause. P8's window end (the next execution on the same target) is the one 1bb already justified for P8.
- R-91 and R-94 are captured, because P8 records every response that refers to R11, whenever it occurs.

**(4) Does it change a scientific prediction?** Yes.
- **P2 (H-B conformance):** H-B becomes easier to falsify, because a non-permitted execution counts even if a response followed. The C1 bearing on H-B changes from "NON-CONFORMS and no response before R-87" to "NON-CONFORMS".
- **P7-HB:** the same.
- **P8:** its domain is extended to deviations of non-conformance.

**(5) Frozen rule.**
> **FR-D6.** A conformance falsifier (P2, P7-HB) = an execution whose operation class is not permitted by the norm in force at t_exec⁻, with no waiver in force at t_exec⁻. Any later response is scored under P8 and never under P2 or P7.
>
> P8 applies to verified failures and to verified deviations, including non-conformance. Its window runs from the deviation's recording time to the next execution trace on the same target. Every response that cites the deviation is recorded; responses outside the window are recorded as LATE_RESPONSE.

## D7: the attestation rule contradicts itself

**(1) Defect, quoted.**
> "The attestation rule contradicts itself. Condition (i) requires an author or process different from the norm-making record, but entry into force is taken from the **adoption record written by the adopter**, which is the status-conferring act. Condition (ii) excludes artefacts that are 'citing that record', but P4 needs uptake artefacts that cite R-89."

**(2) Correction.**
- Separate **being the observation** from **attesting a field of** the observation (§0.5).
- Conditions (i) to (iii) apply only to *attesting* a field.
- The act's own record *is* the observation of the act. It may attest only two fields of that act: who wrote it (as AUTH_ID or ACTOR_SET_ID), and its recording time. It never attests its stated effective date, and never the force of the norm.
- Citing the ruling is allowed for artefacts that are *observations* of uptake (NIF-B, NIF-C, ACT). What is excluded is only the use of a citing artefact's copy of the ruling's self-statements to attest a field.

**(3) Why this is sufficient.**
- The two contradictions came from applying one rule to two roles.
- Once the roles are separated:
  - the adoption record satisfies the rule in the only role it plays (the observation of an adoption, which attests who and when);
  - the uptake artefacts satisfy it in theirs (observations that cite R-89, where the citation is the thing observed).
- No field is attested by a self-report. The stated effective date and the force are never attested by the act itself, so the rule's purpose is kept.

**(4) Does it change a scientific prediction?** No. It fixes a rule's consistency. It does narrow what an adoption record can establish (never the effective date), and this matters for the time premises of P4 and P7.

**(5) Frozen rule.**
> **FR-D7.** A record R of an act is the observation of that act. It may attest (i) its writer identity, graded AUTH_ID or ACTOR_SET_ID, and (ii) its recording time, graded by §0.9. It attests nothing else about itself, including a stated effective date or force.
>
> A field of any *other* observation is independently attested only if its attesting artefact (i) has a writer different from the maker, the adopter and the executor, (ii) does not copy the ruling's self-statements, and (iii) carries a timestamp generated by a system.
>
> Artefacts that cite a ruling are admissible as *observations* of uptake (NIF-B, NIF-C, ACT).

> "**Missing fields**, see JSON `missing_fields`. ## D9: the C1 rule is asymmetric and under-specified

**(1) Defect, quoted.**
> "The C1 rule will probably return UNDETERMINED, and it is asymmetric. If R-72's proviso was unmet but no blocking text covers RED, the rule says UNDETERMINED. By R-72's own logic the conditional authorization never became operative, so the result should be NON-CONFORMS by default. No default reading of 'WP-4B REMAINS BLOCKED' is fixed for the likely case where no scoping text exists. Entry-into-force times for R-77 to R-80 are to come 'from adoption records', but these rulings may not be status-mediated at all, and no fallback is given. The MD and the JSON also scope the 'and' in the CONFORMS branch differently."

**(2) Correction.** (§2)
- **Default state:** WP-4B work is UNAUTHORIZED at 16:10 unless R-72's proviso is *shown* met, by texts in force before 16:10.
- **Default scope:** "WP-4B REMAINS BLOCKED" covers all WP-4B work, including producer-agnostic RED test code, unless a text in force before 16:10 explicitly narrows it.
- **Fallback for rulings that are not status-mediated:** entry into force is not earlier than the ruling's recording time, graded by §0.9. A stated date is SOURCE_STATED.
- **One structure** for CONFORMS: **P ∧ ¬B**. The MD version is kept, because R-72's authorization and R-77's block are separate conditions, and both must be satisfied.
- **UNDETERMINED** is reserved for two cases:
  - required texts cannot be obtained;
  - the time at which a relevant text entered force, relative to 16:10, is NOT_IDENTIFIABLE.
- If the texts are obtained and do not show the proviso met, the result is NON-CONFORMS by default.

**(3) Why this is sufficient.**
- **Asymmetry removed.** The default follows R-72's own conditional form: an authorization that is conditional on a proviso is operative only if the proviso holds. So the case "proviso unmet, no covering block" now yields NON-CONFORMS.
- **Default scope fixed.** The case with no scoping text now has a determinate reading.
- **Fallback added.** Rulings without an adoption record now have a time premise.
- **Consistency.** A single boolean structure makes the MD and the JSON identical.
- **Guard against unseen evidence.** UNDETERMINED remains only where a premise is actually unobservable. So the default is never applied to evidence that has not been seen: missing texts give UNDETERMINED, not NON-CONFORMS.

**(4) Does it change a scientific prediction?** Yes.
- **C1 / P2:** the likely verdict moves from UNDETERMINED to NON-CONFORMS, if R-73..R-76 are obtained and do not show the proviso met.
- **C1 bearing:** changes as in D6. It no longer requires that nothing responded before R-87.
- **G-D1 applies.** If the absence of a permitting text before 16:10 relies on R-81..R-85 having had no force until R-86 adopted them, the result is DISJUNCTIVE {H-D status clause, H-B conformance}.

**(5) Frozen rule.**
> **FR-D9.**
> - **P** = R-72's RED condition and proviso ("no unresolved governance blockers"; the named ARB decisions and scope ruling have landed) are shown met by texts in force before 16:10.
> - **B** = a text in force before 16:10 blocks WP-4B, read by default as covering all WP-4B work including producer-agnostic RED, and no text in force before 16:10 narrows that scope to exclude RED.
>
> Verdicts:
> - **CONFORMS** iff P ∧ ¬B.
> - **NON-CONFORMS** iff the required texts (R-72 to R-80) were obtained and ¬(P ∧ ¬B).
> - **UNDETERMINED** iff a required text could not be obtained, or the entry-into-force time of a text that decides P or B is NOT_IDENTIFIABLE relative to 16:10.
>
> Entry into force: an adoption form, if the ruling is status-mediated; otherwise, not earlier than its recording time. Stated dates are SOURCE_STATED.
>
> The 16:10 time of R11 is itself a git date (SOURCE_STATED). The verdict carries that label.

## D10: the P1 census and the P8 tendency are under-specified

**(1) Defect, quoted.**
> "The P1-HB census refutes only **H-B restricted to window W**, and the spec does not say so. Reading H-B's clause as existential is also an interpretive choice that is not labelled UNKNOWN. Under the other reading ('when the work condition is met, the state changes'), one clean counter-instance would be enough. The P8 'tendency ⇒ census' option gives no threshold, so it cannot be tested."

**(2) Correction.**
- **P1-HB:** label the quantifier reading UNKNOWN, and test both readings:
  - **Reading 1a (existential):** the census over W. A negative result is stated as "H-B reading 1a is not instantiated in W". It is never stated as "H-B refuted".
  - **Reading 1b (conditional-universal):** one eligible target whose work condition is met, and whose state is unchanged by NIF until a separate act, refutes 1b.
- **P8:** drop the tendency reading. No source gives a threshold, and inventing one would be arbitrary. P8 is tested as a universal. If H-B's authors intend a tendency, P8 is declared NOT_TESTABLE_AS_SPECIFIED and is not scored.

**(3) Why this is sufficient.**
- The logical force of each test now matches its quantifier:
  - An existential claim is refuted only by exhausting its domain, so the conclusion is limited to the exhausted domain W.
  - A conditional-universal claim is refuted by one instance.
- Reporting both readings keeps the interpretation from being decided after the fact.
- Dropping the tendency reading removes the only untestable option. Keeping it without a threshold would have left P8 unfalsifiable.

**(4) Does it change a scientific prediction?** Yes.
- **P1-HB:** the conclusion is scoped to W, and a second, stronger test (1b) is added.
- **P8-HB:** only the universal reading remains.

**(5) Frozen rule.**
> **FR-D10.** P1-HB is scored under both readings.
> - 1a: "not instantiated in W" or "instantiated".
> - 1b: FIRED if at least one eligible counter-instance is found (with NIF).
>
> Neither result is generalized beyond W. P8 is universal only. The tendency reading is NOT_TESTABLE_AS_SPECIFIED.

## D11: attestation fields assume artefacts that no input establishes

**(1) Defect, quoted.**
> "The feasibility section is hedged, but the **attestation fields assume** artefacts that no input establishes: CI runs with CI start times; 'server push time' (git history does not record it); 'adopted' R-86 and R-90 (R-90 appears in the inputs in a withdrawal context); adoption records for R-77, R-79 and R-80; 'DA session logs'; version control of IMPLEMENTATION_PROGRESS.md; a register kept as a git file. STATE lists only a register, a few session logs and **one** commit."

**(2) Correction.**
- Phrase every such field as "if such an artefact exists".
- Give a fallback for each, with its grade, in the table in §0.11.
- Mark R-90's status as UNKNOWN.
- Note that git dates (including R11's 16:10) are client-set (§0.9).

**(3) Why this is sufficient.**
- The defect is an existence assumption hidden inside field definitions.
- After the correction, every field is defined whether or not its preferred artefact exists: either the fallback applies with a stated grade, or the field is UNDETERMINED.
- So no result can depend silently on an artefact that no input shows exists.

**(4) Does it change a scientific prediction?** No. Some outcomes are downgraded, for example to FIRED-CONDITIONAL or UNDETERMINED, when the preferred artefacts do not exist.

**(5) Frozen rule.**
> **FR-D11.** Every attestation names a preferred artefact "if it exists", a fallback, and the grade of the fallback (§0.11). A field whose preferred and fallback sources are both missing is UNDETERMINED. The capture reports which artefacts exist.

## D12: P7-HD depends on motive; P8-HD repeats P1

**(1) Defect, quoted.**
> "P7's H-D falsifier ('treated as authorized **because** the predecessor was accepted') depends on motive and cannot be observed as behaviour. It also cannot fire in the R-89 episode, because an authorizing act (R-89) exists. P8's H-D falsifier just repeats P1."

**(2) Correction.**
- **P7-HD:** NOT_APPLICABLE to the R-89 episode.
- **P7-HD in other episodes:** restated in behavioural and NIF terms. NIF shows the successor authorized and in force, and no norm-making act in a complete DCS produced that authorization. This *is* P1 on the gate, and it is scored under P1 only.
- **P8-HD:** points to P1 and is not scored separately.

**(3) Why this is sufficient.**
- The motive clause ("because") is removed, so every remaining condition is observable.
- In the R-89 episode, the premise "no authorizing act" is false by construction, since R-89 exists as a text. So declaring the limb NOT_APPLICABLE is exact.
- Scoring P7-HD and P8-HD under P1 only removes the double counting.

**(4) Does it change a scientific prediction?** Yes.
- **P7-HD:** it is dropped for the R-89 episode, and elsewhere merged into P1.
- **P8-HD:** it is merged into P1.
- H-D's operational predictions are therefore tested only through P1, P4 and P5.

**(5) Frozen rule.**
> **FR-D12.** P7-HD is NOT_APPLICABLE when any norm-making act authorizing the successor exists in the DCS, whatever that act's status. Otherwise, P7-HD and P8-HD are instances of P1-HD and are scored only there.

## D13: the status-mediation upgrade is only partial

**(1) Defect, quoted.**
> "Item 1 (an adoption entry written by the adopter) is still the norm-maker's own act; only its system time and authenticated identity are independent. The behavioural contrast (item 3) is empty unless work was ready and waiting during the prepared interval. As written, the upgrade moves status mediation only **part of the way** to independent observation."

**(2) Correction.** (§3)
- **Item 1:** relabelled as the norm-maker's own act. Only its recording time and its AUTH_ID are independent (FR-D7).
- **New item 0:** NIF-A for status, if Part C finds such a channel.
- **Item 2:** uptake is restricted to NIF-B (third-party application). NIF-C is recorded only.
- **Item 3:** the contrast gets an **eligibility condition**. During the prepared interval, a work item that depends on the ruling was *pending*: its preconditions were met, and it was queued or planned, attested by an artefact with a system-recorded time. A contrast without such an item is VACUOUS and is not scored.
- **Absence of work** in the prepared interval requires a complete execution channel (FR-D5e).

**(3) Why this is sufficient.**
- The upgrade was partial on two counts:
  - Its first item was not independent. The correction now claims only what is independent (time and identity), and it adds the only fully independent source (NIF-A).
  - Its contrast could be vacuous. The eligibility condition ensures that "no execution during the prepared interval" is informative: work was ready, so its absence is a behavioural difference and not a lack of opportunity.

**(4) Does it change a scientific prediction?** Yes, for H-D's status clause (P4). An observed contrast now counts only if it is eligible. H-B's predictions are not affected, because H-B is silent here (SOURCE FACT: IDENTIFIABILITY P4).

**(5) Frozen rule.**
> **FR-D13.** Status mediation counts as independently observed only if:
> - (0) NIF-A records the status transition, **or**
> - (1) an adoption form has a recording time and AUTH_ID, **and** (2) NIF-B uptake follows adoption, **and** (3) an **eligible** contrast is present: pending dependent work existed during the prepared interval, and a complete execution channel shows no execution on it and no NIF-B application before adoption.
>
> Otherwise, status mediation stays SELF_REPORTED or PARTIALLY_INDEPENDENT.

P4 lists R-88's text, which only orders the rulings and says nothing about force. P7's GREEN/VERIFY CI run serves C2's evidence limb, not the gate falsifier. The 'input conflict' may be only apparent: '§WP-4 remains OPEN' may refer to WP-4 as a whole, not WP-4B, and C2's textual order does not establish the order of entry into force."

**(2) Correction.**
